findings: The baseline is about right on average across all counties; its ranges caught the real total in 103 of 210 back-test cases.
The baseline runs 34% high in small counties; its ranges caught the real total in 37 of 75 back-test cases.
The baseline runs 35% low in 'Rural, steady, lower-cost, small' counties; its ranges caught the real total in 3 of 15 back-test cases. Few cases (1 county): read this as a few places, not a pattern.
The baseline is about right on average in rural counties; its ranges caught the real total in 97 of 195 back-test cases.
The baseline runs 14% high in counties with a lower share of Qualified Census Tracts; its ranges caught the real total in 57 of 120 back-test cases.
Its ranges were least reliable in medium counties: they caught the real total in 35 of 75 cases (47%), against the 80% a P10-P90 range aims for.

weakest.phrase: counties with a lower share of Qualified Census Tracts

by_place.limits: Where the baseline itself has been least accurate in past years: small counties (where it has tended to run too high) and counties with a lower share of Qualified Census Tracts (where it has tended to run too high). Read the change in those places with extra care; the Method page shows the back-test.

contest.choosing_rule: Rules whose P10-P90 ranges caught the actual total in 75% to 85% of back-test cases are eligible. Among them the lowest median absolute error is the best; the simplest eligible rule within 5% of that error wins. If no rule is eligible, the rule whose coverage is closest to 80% wins. This rule was fixed in assumptions/backtest.yaml before any score was computed.

rules.describe: simple average of last_5_mean, last_3_mean, median_5, damped_trend, shrink_to_group, top_down_share

bias_correction.rule: Keep the P50 pool-ratio correction only if, out of time, its median absolute error is lower than the uncorrected projection's and its P10-P90 coverage is inside 75%-85%; otherwise drop it. Fixed in assumptions/backtest.yaml (bias_correction) before any score was computed.
bias_correction.reason: the correction did not lower the out-of-time error

variants.definition: all years: every county-year in the Building Permits Survey files, including figures the Census Bureau imputed for offices that did not report; observed only: county-years with any imputed figure removed from both the history a rule reads and the target years it is scored on

statewide.definition: the same rules applied to the state's yearly totals (counties that did not report a year left out of that year); one case per origin; each case's P10-P90 range from the other origins' ratios

origins.note: The 21 rolling origins overlap: each shares up to 4 of its 5 target years with the next. They hold about 5 non-overlapping 5-year periods, so case counts overstate the independent evidence; read coverage and error as resting on about 5 periods, not 21.

stress.sentence: If the next five years look like the 12 past boom periods (origins 1999, 2000, 2001, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019), the baseline's likely range is 5,627 units to 18,161 units (middle 12,243 units).

findings: 7 rules were back-tested on the same 294 county cases. The shrink to place type won: it was typically 47% off, its ranges caught the real total in 49% of cases, and it ran 3% high on average. No rule's coverage was inside the band, so the closest to 80% won.
The five-year mean was typically 48% off and ran 1% high.
The top-down share had the lowest error but did not win: its coverage (48%) was outside the band.

Out of time (each origin corrected only with errors known by then; 182 cases), the winner's own projection was typically 43% off. Correcting it by size class gave 84% with ranges that caught 57%; by place type, 91% and 59%. The engine uses size-class pools: place-type pools did not lower the out-of-time error.
Ranges built from past errors caught the real total less often when tested on later years than when tested on other counties: a new housing cycle moves every county at once.

The winner was chosen on the whole back-test (every origin at once), so the choice itself is in-sample; its ranges and the corrections are scored only with errors from earlier origins. Size classes are worked out at each origin from the years up to it; place types are today's county grouping (current data) applied to every origin.

In 'Rural, steady, lower-cost, small' counties the five-year mean ran 35% low and the shrink to place type runs 35% low; its ranges caught 3 of 15 cases. Few cases: read this as a few places, not a pattern.

bridge.method_text: Carry annual through the gap: the rule's yearly level from the last full year of data is used unchanged for the gap year and each projected year. The gap year is not projected separately and adds nothing to the five-year total.

nowcast.label: 2026 nowcast from monthly year-to-date permits (diagnostic only)
caveats: A year-to-date count is never treated as a full year.
Monthly and annual files differ in reporting and imputation; the share s absorbs that difference as well as the season.
Release dates are the files' Last-Modified dates on the Census server; a re-posted file shows a later date than its first release.
The history files are as posted now; earlier copies were not archived, so this is a revised-data exercise.

state.formula: nowcast = YTD 2026 Jan-Sep / s; YTD = 1,210; s = YTD(y, Jan-Sep) / annual(y) for y in 2021-2025 (2021 0.668, 2022 0.733, 2023 0.746, 2024 0.707, 2025 0.877); low / middle / high use s = 0.877 / 0.733 / 0.668 = 1,380 / 1,651 / 1,811 units; the carried annual level is 2,425 units (state-series mean of 2021-2025; the shipped level comes from county shrinkage).
